add_company_scope:
Add domains/IPs/CIDRs/ICP registrations/company keywords to a company's asset scope. Domains, networks, and ICP registrations automatically claim matching assets; keywords only provide scope hints to Agents.
Company names are unique: create company if it does not exist; otherwise reuse it and merge the scope.
One scope entry per line, automatically recognized as: root domain / URL / individual IP / CIDR network / ICP registration / company keyword.
Always provide reason explaining the attribution evidence (whois/certificate/ASN, etc.).
Guardrails: reject bare TLDs and overly broad networks (IPv4 prefixes must be /16-/32, IPv6 /32-/128); invalid lines are skipped and returned in errors.
add_hint:
Attach strategic hints from the human/main agent to the exploration graph; the planner reads them the next time it generates intents.
★ Prefer batching: submit multiple hints in the hints array (fewer round trips than individual calls). Returns an ids array of the same length and order as hints (failed items have id=0; see errors). For one item, omit hints and provide top-level text.
add_intent:
Generate an exploration direction, write it to the frontier, and connect it to the exploration graph. An intent is an open exploration direction, not a fixed type: freely describe what to explore/verify/exploit in one summary sentence.
★ Prefer batching: submit multiple new directions selected in a round in the intents array (fewer round trips than separate calls). Returns an ids array of the same length and order as intents (failed items have id=0; see errors). For a single item, omit intents and provide the top-level summary.
add_task_hint:
Inject strategic hints into the specified task (its planner reads them when generating intents in the next round).
Prefer batches: submit multiple hints in a single hints array (returns an ids array with the same length and order; failed entries have id=0). For a single hint, omit hints and provide top-level text.
add_task_scope:
Add test scope to this task: it defines the task's authorization boundary and the denominator for asset test coverage.
Supported kind values: company (all company assets) / root_domain (entire root domain and all subdomains) / subdomain (one exact subdomain) / ip / cidr / icp / keyword.
Hosts encountered individually by Workers are automatically added to scope (exact subdomains). This tool deliberately expands scope to an entire root domain/company or adds a specified subdomain/IP.
value: for company, pass an existing company name or id; for root_domain/subdomain, a domain; for ip/cidr, an IP or network; for icp/keyword, a registration number or company keyword.
Always provide reason explaining the auditable basis. Use entries for multiple items.
bind_finding_traffic: Bind additional verified real HTTP traffic to a registered vulnerability. Use the standalone vulnerability record ID for finding_id, not an exploration node ID. All references in a batch succeed or fail together; duplicate references do not overwrite existing notes. Adding bindings marks an existing report as needing an update; do not probe again or create duplicate vulnerabilities just to add traffic.
create_custom_tool: IMPORTANT: After installing tools that the platform does not provide, call this tool to register them so the platform can invoke them. Create a custom tool (shell/command/script/http). shell declares a bash environment tool and requires only key, description, and agents, without exec/schema.
create_mcp: Create an MCP server (stdio/http/sse). After creation, authorize its tools through agent visibility settings.
create_skill: Create a new skill by writing SKILL.md following the agentskills.io specification. The name uses lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
delete_assets_by_host:
Delete assets by exact host: removes its domain/subdomain and associated services and endpoints.
Matches the host exactly after lowercasing and trimming whitespace; no fuzzy or wildcard matching.
A root domain (e.g. example.com) also removes its subdomains and their services/endpoints. A subdomain (e.g. a.example.com) or IP removes only that host and its services/endpoints.
Warning: irreversible hard deletion from the global asset store shared across tasks.
expand_digest: Expand a cold digest: return a compact list of its folded members (id/summary/state/confidence), shaped like the overview's recent_facts/recent_done_intents. Use node_detail(member_id) for full details/evidence of a member.
get_finding_retest_context: Read the vulnerability evidence snapshot, retest status, supplementary notes, and current task constraints associated with the current retest session. No parameters; only the current session can be read.
get_finding_traffic: Read real traffic evidence bound to a finding, regardless of the capture switch. Use the standalone finding record ID returned in report_finding JSON as finding_id, not the exploration node ID on the first line. Omit binding_id initially to retrieve the list and version. An empty list is normal: non-HTTP findings such as TCP issues, or cases without captured traffic, may still use text/command evidence in reports; binding is optional. When bindings exist, read body segments using binding_id, side (request/response), and offset. Pass the retrieved version as evidence_version to update_finding_report, whose finding_id still uses the exploration node ID.
get_task_graph: Read the exploration graph overview of the task specified by task_id (same as graph_overview: asset counts/frontier/findings/coverage, etc.).
get_task_node_detail: Read the full content of an exploration graph node in the specified task (finding/fact/intent/goal: summary and details/evidence/PoC). id is the exploration node id (as returned by report_finding or the id in list_task_findings). Use this to retrieve full vulnerability evidence before writing a report.
get_task_worker_trace: View execution of a work item (intent) in the specified task: get_task_worker_trace(task_id, intent_id) returns step summaries; add step_ids=[...] to retrieve full content for those steps (up to 5 per call; extra ids are ignored after the first 5).
get_worker_output: Get the final output conclusion of an intent (work) in this task or a directly related task. Related-task results include source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. Normal completion returns its summary; stopped/abnormal work returns the last output available before interruption.
goal_met: [Immediately end the entire task] Call only when you have confirmed that all task goals are genuinely achieved and the task as a whole is complete. Achieving just one goal/flag/vulnerability does not count; use prove_goal to mark that individual goal. ⚠️ This does not end a planning round: if there are no new intents to dispatch or you are waiting for worker results, simply end the round without calling this tool (zero intents is completely normal). Normally, prefer prove_goal to prove goals individually; goal_met bypasses individual proofs to conclude the task globally.
graph_overview: (Exploration graph) Distilled exploration status: asset counts, sites without endpoints, frontier, findings, and hints (strategic guidance from the human/main agent, which must inform intent generation). Call this first when planning.
insert_assets:
Register newly discovered assets in a batch; a batch may mix types (see the type enum).
Required fields by type: root_domain→domain; ip→ip (must be IPv4/IPv6, not a hostname); subdomain→domain; app→app_name; service(HTTP)→url; service(non-HTTP)→service_name+port (at least one of ip/domain); endpoint→url+method. See each field description for other fields.
auth/technologies/params are merged by appending, without overwriting existing values.
Returns: {results:[{index,id,type}], errors:[{index,error}]}
kill_work: Terminate a running intent (work). Use to stop misguided or pointless exploration; the terminated intent is marked stopped and will not be automatically claimed again. Inspect its activity with get_worker_output before deciding.
list_assets:
Query the asset store by DSL expression or directly by id/ids; supports pagination. Returns only assets in the test scope of this task and directly linked tasks.
DSL: field=value fuzzy (ILIKE) | field==value exact | field!=value exclude | numeric fields support > >= < <= | bare terms = full-text fuzzy search; combine with AND/OR (AND has higher precedence), with parentheses for grouping. Use the separate type parameter for asset type, not the DSL.
Without id/ids, dsl must not be empty (unfiltered queries for all assets are not allowed).
Available fields: domain (root/subdomain/service domain), root_domain, ip, url, page_title, icp, service_name, app_name, method (e.g. GET/POST), service_type (http|other), record_type (e.g. A/CNAME), technology (array; = fuzzy, == exact), port/status_code/company_id (integers).
Examples: status_code>=400 AND technology=shiro; (port==80 OR port==443) AND technology=nginx
list_companies: List companies in the asset store with their asset scope and attributed asset count. Use this to discover companies and obtain company_id (used to associate apps in insert_assets and filter list_assets by company_id). Optionally filter company names with case-insensitive fuzzy search; leave empty to return all.
list_facts: Paginate exploration facts/conclusions in this task and directly related tasks, newest first (compact: id+summary+state; long summaries are truncated; use node_detail(id) for full text). All parameters are optional: limit (default 20, max 100), before (cursor; pass next_before from the previous page to fetch older entries; omitted/0 = latest page), q (filter by summary keyword). Returns {facts, total, has_more, next_before}: total is the filtered count; when has_more=true, continue with next_before. Related-task entries include source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. Use list_findings for vulnerabilities.
list_findings: List confirmed vulnerabilities in this task and directly related tasks (compact: id+task_id+intent_id+vulnclass+severity+summary+state). Related-task entries include source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. Includes vulnerabilities only; use list_facts for ordinary exploration facts and node_detail(id) for details.
list_goals: List this task's goal nodes and their states (open/met) to assess completion.
list_llm_profiles: List available LLM profiles: id, name, model, format, and whether currently active. Pass the id as llm_profile_id to spawn_task to select a dedicated LLM for the child task (for example, a cheaper model for reconnaissance and a stronger model for exploitation). API keys are not included.
list_task_findings: Read confirmed vulnerabilities for the task specified by task_id (including flags/PoCs; each includes id/task_id/intent_id/vulnclass/severity/summary/status).
list_task_worker_traces: List work items (intents) executed in the specified task and their step counts to identify items worth reviewing with get_task_worker_trace.
list_tasks: List all tasks (id/description/goal/status/runtime/parent task/LLM profile) so the orchestration agent can see the overall state, identify stalled tasks, and check which LLM each uses. Runtime in seconds: running = creation to now; terminal = creation to last activity. llm_profile is the profile name used by the task planner/worker; (active profile) follows the globally active profile.
list_untested_assets:
List assets within this task and directly linked tasks that are not yet covered by fact anchors (linked scope is read-only; decide for yourself whether additional testing is needed).
Optionally filter by asset type: root_domain/subdomain/service/app/endpoint/ip.
Pagination: page starts at 1; page_size defaults to 10. Returns {assets:[{id,type,label}], total, page, page_size}. Available only in task context.
node_detail: Get the complete exploration graph node by id from this task or directly related tasks. Inherited nodes include source_task_id/inherited=true and are read-only. Accepts only exploration node IDs returned by list_facts/list_findings/graph_overview; use list_assets/asset_neighbors for assets.
pause_task: Pause the specified task (stop its planner/worker loops).
prove_goal: Call when a finding/fact proves a goal has been achieved: connect the evidence node to the goal and mark it met.
record_fact:
Write exploration facts/conclusions to the exploration graph and connect them to the intent that produced them (intent_id). Records exploration results, including positive conclusions such as fingerprints/enumeration, and negative conclusions such as 'port closed', 'parameter not injectable', or 'no login entry found'.
⚠️ Consolidate multiple observations from one exploration into one fact whenever possible, rather than splitting them: summary = one sentence summarizing the conclusion; detail = related details (which may include multiple items). Example: a fingerprinting intent yields one fact {summary:'Identified site X technology stack and response characteristics', detail:'nginx 1.25 / Vue3 / 200 / title=.. / body_len=..'}, rather than separate facts for status code, fingerprint, and title. An intent usually produces one fact; excessive splitting makes the graph grow without bound.
★ Use the facts array to write multiple distinct conclusions in one call (each may omit intent_id to use the top-level default). Returns an ids array of the same length and order as facts.
⚠️ Record only conclusions you actually observed in tool output; do not invent details. evidence and confidence prevent inaccurate conclusions from polluting the graph:
  · evidence = one line of key evidence supporting the conclusion (command plus the one or two most probative output lines). **Keep it concise**: details already belong in detail, so do not paste long output here.
  · confidence = observed (directly seen in output) | inferred (deduced from observations).
  · For **negative conclusions** (not injectable/port closed/no entry found, etc.), record only "observation + tentative interpretation": state what you actually saw and let the planner decide globally whether to abandon the direction. Always provide evidence. Mark inferred if methods are not exhausted or evidence is weak (including a single probe or apparent behavior); use observed only when methods are exhausted and the result is directly observed.
record_finding_retest_result: Save a single conclusion for the current retest session; the original vulnerability evidence and report remain unchanged. When the session completes successfully with a fixed conclusion, the system automatically marks the vulnerability as fixed; other conclusions preserve its original status. Provide evidence from the actual checks performed; if verification is not possible, explain what blocked it.
report_finding: Record a confirmed vulnerability, providing verifiable evidence such as command output and logs in evidence. In task context, pass the current intent_id. The returned finding_id is the independent vulnerability record ID; finding_node_id is the exploration node ID (the first line retains that node number).
search_all_worker_traces: [Usually not recommended because the system already supplies most information] Search other work's execution traces in this task by keyword (q), to recover something a worker saw but did not record in a fact (a path/token/error, etc.).Steps from your own intent are automatically excluded (they are already in your context).Returns only matching step summaries (summary≤100 characters), each with intent_id; use get_worker_trace(intent_id, step_ids=[...]) to retrieve full content.
search_task_worker_traces: Search execution traces of all work items in the specified task by keyword (returns matching step summaries and intent_id).
set_constraints:
Add operating constraints to this task to define exploration boundaries: type=allow (permitted operations) or deny (prohibited operations).
A constraint defines which operations are permitted/prohibited (e.g. 'test only the current port; do not scan other ports', 'do not write to the production database', 'passive reconnaissance only'); it is neither a goal nor an attack step.
★ Prefer batching: submit multiple constraints in the constraints array; returned ids have the same length and order (failed items have id=0; see errors). For one item, omit constraints and provide top-level text/type.
Register only constraints explicitly stated in the task goal/description; do not invent them. When unsure of the type, use deny (more conservative).
set_goals:
Add exploration goals to this task. A goal is a final deliverable/verifiable result, not an attack step or reconnaissance action.
★ Prefer batching: submit multiple goals in the goals array; returned ids have the same length and order (failed items have id=0; see errors). For one item, omit goals and provide the top-level text.
vulnclass is optional: the associated vulnerability class (e.g. SQLi/IDOR); leave empty for business-logic goals. The system assesses achievement and marks goals met; this tool only adds them.
spawn_task: Create a child task and start its exploration engine, returning task_id. Use this to delegate one item (such as a challenge or goal) as an independent task. Optional parent_ref: the parent task id associated with the current orchestration, to establish a parent-child relationship.
steer_work: Inject a steering instruction into a running intent (work) in real time without interruption or lost progress: the worker receives it before its next action and adjusts accordingly. Use for corrections within an intent, such as 'stop doing X, focus on Y'. If the entire direction is wrong, use kill_work and issue a new intent. First inspect its activity with get_worker_output.
traffic_blob: Read large raw request/response bodies in chunks. Content shown by traffic_get as '…[truncated] @blob sha256:<hash>' is stored here; pass that hash to retrieve the full content. Returns up to 8KB per call; use offset to continue (the result includes total length). Suitable for backup files, exposed source code, large JSON exports, and other responses exceeding the inline threshold.
traffic_get: Get the raw request/response of captured traffic by id (truncated if too large). Use with traffic_search to avoid repeating curl requests.
traffic_search: Query target traffic captured by the recording proxy (host is required; accepts a bare host, host:port, or full URL, with optional URL-substring or body-keyword filters). Specifying a port returns only that service, avoiding mixed traffic from other ports on the same IP. body_contains searches captured request/response headers and bodies, supporting arbitrary substrings and Chinese text (at least 3 characters). Returns only a lightweight index (id/method/url/status/resp_len), without response content. For nonempty results, verify each request/response with traffic_get before passing IDs that actually support the current finding to bind_finding_traffic. Defaults to 3 results, maximum 10 per page; use page for more.
update_custom_tool: Modify an existing custom tool by key.
update_finding_report: Write or update a detailed report for a registered vulnerability (full Markdown, replacing all previous content). Pass the id returned by report_finding as finding_id (the number in "finding recorded: <id>"). Recommended sections: vulnerability overview, impact, reproduction steps, evidence/PoC, and remediation.
update_mcp: Modify an existing MCP server by ID.
update_skill_file: Write or overwrite a file in a skill (defaults to SKILL.md). Use this to edit instructions or add scripts/references.
